Google Search Guidance on Generative AI Content
A Guide to Google Search Ranking Systems
In-depth Guide to How Google Search Works

records.statement: Google Search Essentials describes technical requirements, spam policies and key best practices. Eligibility is not a guarantee of crawling, indexing or serving. Create helpful, reliable, people-first content and follow structured-data guidance.
records.applicability: Google Search policy and documented principles

records.statement: Google spam policies describe behaviors that can lead to lower ranking or omission from Search. Content should provide the best experience for people and uphold the principles of Search.
records.applicability: Google Search policy and documented principles

records.statement: Google guidance describes helpful, reliable, people-first content and asks whether content is created primarily to help people rather than manipulate Search.
records.applicability: Google Search policy and documented principles

records.statement: Google Search guidance on generative AI focuses on using automation responsibly and ensuring content is helpful, accurate, relevant and not created primarily to manipulate rankings.
records.applicability: Google Search policy and documented principles

records.statement: Google AI Overviews and AI Mode use the same foundational SEO best practices as Google Search. There are no additional technical requirements or special optimizations required for inclusion; pages must be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet.
records.applicability: Applicable standard or vocabulary; not a ranking claim

records.statement: Google ranking systems use automated systems and many signals to present relevant useful results. The guide describes notable systems and explains that systems and updates evolve; it is documentation of systems, not a promise of a ranking outcome.
records.applicability: Applicable standard or vocabulary; not a ranking claim

records.statement: Google Search works through crawling, indexing and serving results. Google does not guarantee crawling, indexing or serving even when Search Essentials are followed.
records.applicability: Applicable standard or vocabulary; not a ranking claim

records.statement: Google structured-data documentation explains how markup helps Search understand page content. Eligibility for a supported feature must be established from Google's feature documentation; vocabulary alone is not a guarantee of a rich result.
records.applicability: Google Search policy and documented principles

records.statement: Bing Webmaster guidance is a secondary search-engine perspective. It may corroborate durable search practices but cannot override Google-specific policy.
records.applicability: Bing Search perspective; not Google policy

records.statement: Schema.org defines shared vocabulary types and properties for structured data. Vocabulary semantics do not establish support by a particular search engine.
records.applicability: Applicable standard or vocabulary; not a ranking claim

records.statement: W3C WAI publishes accessibility standards and guidance for accessible web content. Accessibility guidance is a web standard and must not be represented as a direct Google ranking-factor claim.
records.applicability: Applicable standard or vocabulary; not a ranking claim
